title: feat(wire): post a selected DXF circle or racetrack punch with native arcs
body:
Stacked on #2974. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/04cec49fe...issue/2022-agie-placed-dxf).

Process change: yes

This PR now uses the #2984 zero-step setup writer and the #3180 selected-chain wire path. The port merged `04cec49fe` (#2974) into the branch. The branch merges cleanly with `main` (`git merge-tree`, no conflicts).

## What changed

A Wire Contour punch can use one selected closed DXF chain that is a circle or a racetrack. A racetrack has two straight lines that are tangent to two semicircles of the same radius. The native wire EDM post writes the nominal arcs as `G03` blocks with incremental `I`/`J` centres.

- `camcraft_geometry::wire_round_profile`: `RoundProfile::from_chain` reads the selected chain and proves the tangent joins, the radius and the joint gap. `preview()` gives a polygon that encloses each true arc with at most 0.000025 mm of radial excess.
- `operation/wire_sketch.rs`: `nominal_ring` gives the preview polygon to the generator and to the wire laws for a punch. A straight chain and a die keep the old behaviour. A die with arcs is still refused.
- `operation/agie_profile.rs`: the existing checks moved into `checked()`, with the same messages and order. `agie_sketch_job` adds the DXF punch. It checks the rest of the drawing against the native envelope (arc extrema plus 0.4 mm, and the full threading hole).
- `posting_agie.rs`: one selected DXF chain goes to `agie::export_round_with_review`. Other jobs use the group path as before.
- `post/src/agie/round_profile.rs`: native ISO blocks, the arc envelope bound and the refusals. The SBL and SBR come from `PunchSetup20::encode`.
- The examples select the closed chain through `list_features` and `set_operation_geometry`. They use the post name `Native wire EDM job files`.

Dropped from the old branch: the whole-drawing source (`SrcRef::Entity`) and its stamp, which #3180 replaces. Also dropped: the prism mesh, the `round_profile` field on `AgieJob` and the `jescript.rs` writer. The decision file has the reasons.

## Scope

In scope, as the control data of this PR supports:

- One racetrack punch with straight sides parallel to X or Y, and a perpendicular entry on a straight side.
- One circle punch from R6 to R15 with a horizontal or vertical radial entry.
- A 20 mm plate, a single work, and coordinates exactly on the five-decimal grid.

Out of scope, and refused visibly:

- A die opening with arcs (needs `c_die` and a control run).
- Other plate heights.
- A group with an arc work (`PunchGroup20` reads modeled punches only).
- Oblique racetracks and oblique holes (need a rounding proof and a control run).
- Laser work and other drawings of #2022.

## Setup field sources

No setup field is new. The SBL is `PunchSetup20::encode`, the control-checked `CCSEP20` punch of #2984. A test compares each SBL with `CCSEP20.SBL`: only the stem and the `stp1` position change. The stock (80 × 60 × 20 mm), the holes and the geometry come from the examples of this PR.

## Readings

Emulated Agie Classic Cut 2S, clone of `practice-color.qcow2` (SHA-256 `b827a383…` unchanged; clone deleted). Four jobs from head `124be7caf`: `RACE20`, `CIRCLE20` (R10, hole X−17 Y0), `NORTH15` (R15, hole X0 Y22) and `EAST6` (R6, hole X13 Y0). For each job:

- The ISO and SBL bytes on the guest are identical to the export.
- The tree shows `CCB030[0]` after import. FORMALCHECK gives one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- The quality is CCB030 with Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0 and Te 1.5. The TECCUT header is Dia 0.25, H20, Ra 0.30 (row 0199, `estbca25nnn060b030020`).
- After TECCUT: `CCB030[4]`, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm, and `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. The warnings are `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.

GRAFICHECK (J00):

- `RACE20`: all passes keep the arc centres (10, 1) and (−6, 1). The pass radii are 10.245, 10.155, 10.140 and 10.134 mm. The trims run in the opposite direction (`G02`). The separation on the straight is 1.000 mm (X2 to X1).
- Circles: all passes are concentric on (0, 0). The separation arc ends 1/R radians from the seam (0.100, 0.0667 and 0.1667 rad), a nominal arc of 1.000 mm.

These readings agree with the earlier control readings of this PR. No physical cut was made.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/agie_native/dxf.rs`:
  - `a_translated_and_rotated_racetrack_posts_two_exact_g03_caps`: golden `RACE20.ISO`, and the SBL against `CCSEP20.SBL`.
  - `a_circle_starts_at_its_radial_seam_and_keeps_the_setup_of_the_checked_punch`: golden `CIRCLE20.ISO`, and the SBL.
  - `other_drawing_geometry_must_clear_the_native_rough_pass_and_wire`.
  - `a_moved_open_tall_or_misplaced_racetrack_publishes_nothing`.
  - `a_nonradial_hole_or_unqualified_circle_radius_publishes_nothing`.
- `crates/post/src/agie/round_profile_tests.rs`: the diameter ends for R6, R8.375, R10 and R15 in four directions, the ISO text of the circle and the racetrack, the arc envelope bound at exactly 0.4 mm, the refusals, and no files after a refusal.
- `crates/geometry/src/wire_round_profile/tests.rs`: the chain reading and the preview bounds.
- `wire_dxf_selection::curved_pick_survives_but_generic_generation_refuses_and_undo_restores_the_pick` is updated. A punch circle now passes the round-profile check, and a die with arcs keeps the old refusal.
- The goldens that main has (CCSEP20, DIE20 and the inspection goldens) are unchanged. The other goldens are additions; see "Goldens moved". The `agie_native` suite and the `camcraft-post` agie tests pass.

## Gate (head `7e490d7c2`)

The head merges `origin/main` at `aedd9750c` (through the #2974 head), which has the fix of #3774.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the geometry change selects the batch fallback. 1201 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (40.8 min), at a 1-minute load average under 25 at the start. The plan included `agie_native`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `example_catalog` (with `catalog_3d_rough_finish`), `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`. All passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main`: clean.
- This is a P4 PR, so no heavy step ran.

## Not exercised

- A physical cut.
- A racetrack with a radius other than R10 on the control.
- The GUI chain pick. The examples and tests use the MCP and script path.

Effort: high
Changelog: A selected DXF circle or racetrack chain can drive a Wire Contour punch, and the native wire EDM job writes its nominal arcs as G03 blocks.

## UI screenshots

This PR contains the two open-cutoff controls of #2972 on the Wire Contour Passes tab. One pair of images covers all five PRs of the stack. The reviewer rendered the images with the crate's egui_kittest harness.

Before (main):

![Before: Wire Contour Passes tab on main](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr-2972/wire-open-cutoff-before.png?raw=true)

After (with the two cutoff controls):

![After: Wire Contour Passes tab with the two cutoff controls](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr-2972/wire-open-cutoff-after.png?raw=true)

## Goldens moved

The golden files below are additions relative to main. This PR changes no golden file that main already has. The goldens CCSEP20 and DIE20 of main do not change.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/CIRCLE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of a placed circle DXF job. Added by #2978 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/RACE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of a placed racetrack DXF job. Added by #2978 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/LOWER20.SBL` (A): pins the open-cutoff (zero-step, one cut) setup SBL. Added by #2972 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/PAIR20.SBL` (A): pins the SBL of a group of two punches on one plate. Added by #2974 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/PAIR20.SBR` (A): pins the SBR of a group of two punches on one plate. Added by #2974 of the stack.

## Test layout

This PR adds no new top-level test binary. The post setup tests of the stack are modules of an existing suite. The test count did not change.

- `crates/post/tests/agie_cutoff_setup.rs` (from #2972) moved to `crates/post/tests/agie_safe_setup/cutoff.rs`: module `cutoff` of `agie_safe_setup`, 4 tests.
- `crates/post/tests/agie_group_setup.rs` (from #2974) moved to `crates/post/tests/agie_safe_setup/group.rs`: module `group` of `agie_safe_setup`, 4 tests. The suite now has 16 tests (8 + 4 + 4).
- The tests are unchanged except for the golden paths (`../golden/`). The Gate map of `agie_safe_setup` covers `camcraft_post::agie_setup`, so the quick gate selects the suite for a change in the setup writer.
- The app tests of this PR were already the module `dxf` of `agie_native`.
